facts.title: Arthur L. Irving Institute for Energy and Society
facts.nameOnPage: Irving Institute for Energy and Society
facts.summary: Dartmouth's energy institute, described as a hub of collaboration that prepares the next generation of energy experts.
facts.hook: connects students to a collaborative hub preparing the next generation of energy experts
facts.quote: Irving Institute for Energy and Society: A hub of collaboration preparing the next generation of energy experts.
facts.commonnessReason: Dartmouth's main energy institute, familiar to applicants interested in energy.

facts.title: Dartmouth Center for Social Impact
facts.summary: Dartmouth's center for community-driven experiential learning, which prepares students to address pressing societal problems.
facts.hook: offers community-driven experiential learning aimed at pressing societal problems
facts.quote: The Dartmouth Center for Social Impact educates students to be transformative leaders for the common good. Through community-driven experiential learning, our students cultivate their skills, scholarship, and passion to develop high-impact approaches to the most pressing societal problems.
facts.sourceTitle: Mission and Vision | Students | Social Impact
facts.commonnessReason: The college's main service and community engagement center.

facts.title: Institute of Arctic Studies
facts.summary: An institute that offers interdisciplinary research opportunities, discussion, and education in polar studies.
facts.hook: offers interdisciplinary research opportunities and education in polar studies
facts.quote: Institute of Arctic Studies: Provides interdisciplinary research opportunities, discussion, and education in polar studies, highlighting the importance of polar regions.
facts.commonnessReason: A named institute on Dartmouth's main Centers & Institutes page, known to applicants interested in polar studies.

facts.title: John Sloan Dickey Center for International Understanding
facts.summary: A center that brings the world to Dartmouth through dialogue, experiential education, and engagement on international policy and diplomacy.
facts.hook: engages students in international policy and diplomacy through dialogue and experiential education
facts.quote: Through informed and impactful dialogue, experiential education, and engagement on pressing issues in international policy and diplomacy, The Dickey Center brings the world to Dartmouth and Dartmouth to the world to engage with today's great issues.
facts.sourceTitle: Dickey Center for International Understanding - Dickey Center for International Understanding at Dartmouth
facts.commonnessReason: One of Dartmouth's best-known centers; internationally minded applicants often cite it.

facts.title: Magnuson Center for Entrepreneurship
facts.summary: Dartmouth's entrepreneurship center, which supports students along the entrepreneurial journey with hands-on learning, mentorship, events, and resources.
facts.hook: supports students at every stage of the entrepreneurial journey with hands-on learning, mentorship, and events
facts.quote: Our mission is to serve Dartmouth students, alumni, faculty, and staff along all points of the entrepreneurial journey through hands-on learning, mentorship, events, and resources.
facts.commonnessReason: The college's main entrepreneurship center.

facts.title: Native American Program
facts.summary: A program that supports Indigenous students with holistic support and dedicated living-learning spaces, and partners across Dartmouth to uphold its founding charter.
facts.hook: supports Indigenous students with holistic support and dedicated living-learning spaces
facts.quote: The Native American Program champions Indigenous students through holistic support ... and dedicated living-learning spaces. The program partners with faculty, staff, and student organizations across the institution to uphold Dartmouth's founding charter through collaboration, training, and educational opportunities.
facts.commonnessReason: A well-known part of Dartmouth's identity and history.

facts.title: Nelson A. Rockefeller Center for Public Policy and the Social Sciences
facts.summary: Dartmouth's public policy center, which trains students through policy and social science education, public lectures with visiting scholars and practitioners, policy research, and skills training.
facts.hook: trains students in public policy through education, policy research, and skills training
facts.quote: The Rockefeller Center educates, trains, and inspires the next generation of public policy leaders, across fields, through multidisciplinary policy and social science-focused education, engagements and public lectures with distinguished visiting scholars and practitioners, policy-oriented research across the social sciences, and skills training.
facts.sourceTitle: Dartmouth College - The Nelson A. Rockefeller Center for Public Policy
facts.commonnessReason: One of Dartmouth's best-known centers and a frequent reference in Why Dartmouth essays.

facts.title: ENGS 21: Introduction to Engineering
facts.summary: The introductory engineering course, in which students work as a team on a complete design project applied to a real problem from initial concept to final recommendations.
facts.hook: puts students on a team design project that takes a real problem from initial concept to final recommendations
facts.quote: The student is introduced to engineering through participation, as a member of a team, in a complete design project. ... Engineering principles of analysis, experimentation, and design are applied to a real problem, from initial concept to final recommendations.
facts.commonnessReason: The required gateway design course for the engineering major, so engineering applicants often mention it.

facts.title: ENGS 28: Embedded Systems
facts.summary: An embedded systems course that introduces physical sensors and actuators and how to connect them to a microcontroller, for students ready to go beyond hobby-level work with boards like Arduino.
facts.hook: introduces sensors, actuators, and microcontroller interfacing beyond hobby-level Arduino projects
facts.quote: Many students have been exposed to the potential of embedded systems at the hobby or maker level through robotics and the boards such as the popular Arduino and are excited to go farther. ... Engs 28 will introduce you to a variety of physical sensors and actuators, and how to connect them to a microcontroller.

facts.title: ENGS 37: Introduction to Environmental Engineering
facts.summary: A survey of the sources, measurement techniques, and treatment technologies for pollution, covering water pollution, air pollution, solid wastes, and pollutant fate and transport.
facts.hook: introduces the sources, measurement, and treatment of water and air pollution
facts.quote: A survey of the sources, measurement techniques, and treatment technologies relating to environmental pollution resulting from the activities of humans. ... Technological and other issues will be addressed relating to water pollution, air pollution, solid wastes, and the fate and transport of pollutants in the environment.

facts.title: ENGS 42: Watershed Hydrology
facts.summary: A course on how water and sediment move through watersheds, including runoff, streamflow, and the transport and fate of contaminants, taught through field and computational methods.
facts.hook: trains students to make field measurements and analyze environmental data on runoff, streamflow, and contaminants
facts.quote: The processes controlling the generation of runoff and streamflow are highlighted and used to explore the transport and fate of sediment and contaminants in watersheds. Throughout the course, ideas and concepts are explored through field and computational methods, with emphasis given to developing observational skills, making field measurements, and doing environmental data analysis.

facts.title: ENGS 45: Sustainable Urban Systems (Berlin)
facts.summary: An engineering course on the technology of urban sustainability, from energy, air quality, and water supply to transportation, decarbonization, and city planning.
facts.hook: examines how cities handle energy, air quality, water, transportation, and decarbonization through an engineering lens
facts.quote: This engineering course addresses the technological aspects of urban sustainability, including energy procurement, energy consumption and green energy, air quality, water supply, use and treatment, building infrastructure, transportation, resource conservation, decarbonization, city planning and the role of automation and information technology in modern sustainable cities.

facts.title: ENGS 85.16: Energy and Climate Systems Analysis and Decision Making
facts.summary: A course on decision analysis and systems modeling for energy systems and climate change mitigation, in which students apply these tools to a real-world case study with local or regional stakeholders.
facts.hook: applies decision analysis and energy-climate models to a real case study with local or regional stakeholders
facts.quote: This course introduces the principles of decision analysis and systems modeling, with a focus on energy systems and climate change mitigation applications. ... To bridge theory and practice, students will apply these tools to a real-world case study in partnership with local or regional stakeholders.

facts.title: ENVS 21: Transforming the Energy System: Keeping the Lights on While Saving the Planet
facts.summary: A course on the shift to renewable energy in New England as a response to climate change that culminates in a discussion of Dartmouth's own energy transition.
facts.hook: studies New England's renewable energy transition and ends by examining Dartmouth's own energy transition
facts.quote: This course will explore how transitioning to renewable energy systems is a necessary leverage point for addressing human-caused climate change, with a specific focus on how energy for electricity and heat is generated and used in New England. ... The course will culminate in a discussion of Dartmouth's own energy transition as well as regional- and national scale solutions

facts.title: ENVS 50: Environmental Problem Analysis and Policy Formulation
facts.summary: A course in which student groups formulate policy measures for a local environmental problem and present and defend their recommendations publicly.
facts.hook: has student teams craft and publicly defend policy recommendations for a local environmental problem
facts.quote: Students working together in groups will formulate and justify policy measures that they think would be appropriate to deal with a local environmental problem. ... Considerable field work may be involved, and the final examination will consist of a public presentation and defense of student-generated policy recommendations.

facts.title: GEOG 28: Immigration, Race, and Ethnicity
facts.summary: A geography course on 20th-century U.S. immigration that pays special attention to race and ethnicity, nativist reactions, and differences among Latino, Asian, and European groups.
facts.hook: examines U.S. immigration and differences among Latino, Asian, and European immigrant groups
facts.quote: This course examines 20th century immigration to the United States and pays special attention to issues of race and ethnicity. ... We feature nativist reactions to immigration and highlight differences within and between Latino, Asian, and European groups throughout the course.

facts.title: GEOG 42: Water Policy and Politics
facts.summary: A course on the political, social, and legal aspects of water resource management that shows how hydrology plays out in a socio-political arena.
facts.hook: shows how the technical side of hydrology plays out in water policy and politics
facts.quote: This course is designed to provide students with a general background to the issues confronting water resource management. The course covers the political, social and legal aspects confronting effective water policy decision making. One of the goals is to demonstrate that the technical aspects of hydrology occur within a socio-political arena.

facts.title: GEOG 57: Urban Applications of GIS
facts.summary: A geography course on using GIS to solve urban problems in planning and design, public administration, environmental assessment, land use change, and social and political issues.
facts.hook: teaches students to apply GIS to urban planning, land use, and public administration problems
facts.quote: This course is about how to use GIS technology to solve urban problems. The application problems that will be discussed in the class are from areas including urban planning and design, public administration, business decision-making, environment assessment, land use change, and social and political issues.

facts.title: GEOG 62.01: River Processes and Watershed Science
facts.summary: A course on how watershed processes supply water and sediment to stream channels and how climate change is shifting watershed and river processes.
facts.hook: connects watershed processes and river sediment to the effects of climate change
facts.quote: This course examines the links between watershed scale processes such as weathering, denudation, and mass wasting on the supply of water and sediment to stream channels on both contemporary and geologic timescales and further evaluates the role of climate change on the magnitude and direction of shifts in watershed and fluvial processes.

facts.title: MUS 35: The Jazz Language
facts.summary: A course that presents the essential jazz vocabulary to instrumentalists and vocalists, who learn phrases by ear and transcribe them in all 12 keys.
facts.hook: trains jazz players to learn phrases by ear and transcribe them in all 12 keys
facts.quote: This course will present the essential elements of the "jazz vocabulary" to instrumentalists and vocalists. ... Students will practice learning phrases by ear, which they will then transcribe and write in 12-keys.

facts.title: SPAN 73.14: Embodying Care: Immigration, Health, and the Medical Humanities
facts.summary: A seminar in which students use fiction, theatre, art, documentary, and community-engaged methods to study immigrant health in U.S. and Latinx contexts and produce bilingual, public-facing work.
facts.hook: has students study immigrant health in Latinx communities and produce bilingual, public-facing work
facts.quote: Through fiction, theatre, visual art, documentary, and community-engaged methods, students examine immigrant health in U.S. and Latinx contexts and produce bilingual, public-facing work that connects analysis to practice.

facts.title: SPAN 9.02: Culture and Conversation: Spanish for Health Equity
facts.summary: A Spanish course for health and medical settings that examines language and intercultural proficiency in health care access and includes a Social Impact Practicum.
facts.hook: builds Spanish for health settings and examines how language shapes access to care, with a community practicum
facts.quote: The goal is to expand foundational communication skills so that students can use Spanish in academic and professional settings in health and medical fields, and so that they can reflect critically on the role of linguistic and intercultural proficiency in health care access (particularly in the United States). ... it includes a Social Impact Practicum in collaboration with the Center for Social Impact.

facts.title: Dartmouth Brain Imaging Center
facts.summary: A research facility with an MRI machine used only for research and available to students and faculty studying neuroscience topics.
facts.hook: gives students studying neuroscience access to a research-only MRI facility
facts.quote: Dartmouth Brain Imaging Center: Houses an MRI machine used strictly for research and available to students and faculty studying a wide range of topics related to neuroscience.
facts.commonnessReason: Featured on Dartmouth's main Centers & Institutes page and familiar to neuroscience applicants.

facts.title: Dartmouth Organic Farm
facts.summary: An educational farm three miles north of campus, on conservation land whose growing field borders trails along the Connecticut River, used for hands-on and interdisciplinary learning.
facts.hook: offers hands-on, interdisciplinary learning on a college farm beside the Connecticut River
facts.quote: Since then, the O Farm (as it is lovingly called by students) has grown into a hub for hands-on and interdisciplinary learning at Dartmouth. ... The O Farm is 3 miles north of the main Dartmouth campus, at 104 Lyme Road (Rt. 10) in Hanover. It is situated on conservation easement land, and our growing field abuts public-access walking trails along the Connecticut River.
facts.commonnessReason: A known campus resource for environmentally minded students.

facts.title: Hood Museum of Art
facts.summary: Dartmouth's teaching museum, which aims to create a learning environment for transformative encounters with works of art.
facts.hook: uses a teaching museum to bring students into direct encounters with works of art
facts.quote: Hood Museum of Art: A teaching museum that creates an ideal learning environment that fosters transformative encounters with works of art.
facts.commonnessReason: A flagship campus institution that many applicants mention.

facts.title: MShop at Dartmouth
facts.summary: An instructional machine shop with machining and fabrication equipment where staff teach hands-on skills to students with no experience.
facts.hook: teaches machining and fabrication to students who have never used a tool
facts.quote: No experience necessary. ... The MShop is a unique instructional workshop where problem-solving and teamwork skills are fostered through hands-on learning. ... Browse our extensive array of machining and fabrication equipment. Never even used a tool before? We'll teach you everything you need to know.
facts.sourceTitle: MShop – Overview of the machines available for use, along with related operating manuals and other useful information.

facts.title: Project Spaces & Labs (Dartmouth Engineering)
facts.summary: Thayer's instructional labs and workshops, which support the project-based curriculum with hands-on engineering projects and design and fabrication for research.
facts.hook: gives students hands-on space and staff support for real-world engineering projects
facts.quote: The instructional labs and workshops, and their staff, support Dartmouth's project-based curriculum. The goal is to give students hands-on experiences with real-world engineering projects, as well as provide support for faculty and students involved in design and fabrication for research.

facts.title: Rauner Special Collections Library
facts.summary: Dartmouth's special collections library, holding over 100,000 rare books, millions of manuscripts, and the College Archives, with a team that partners with students on research.
facts.hook: partners with students on research using rare books, manuscripts, and the College Archives
facts.quote: Stewarded by a team of specialists, Rauner Special Collections Library houses over 100,000 rare books, millions of manuscripts, and the extensive Dartmouth College Archives. The team collaborates and partners with students, faculty, staff, and the archive-curious at Dartmouth—and across the globe—to accelerate research and advance scholarship.
facts.sourceTitle: Rauner Special Collections Library | Dartmouth Libraries
facts.commonnessReason: A well-known library that humanities applicants often mention.

facts.title: Student Workshops at the Hop
facts.summary: Woodworking, jewelry and metal, and ceramics studios at the Hopkins Center where students build hands-on projects without prior experience.
facts.hook: opens woodworking, metal, and ceramics studios to students with no experience
facts.quote: Hone your craft with hands-on projects in wood, metal/jewelry and clay—no experience needed! ... This workshop allows students to try their hands at furniture design, cabinetmaking, wood turning, carving and all aspects of woodworking.
facts.sourceTitle: Student Workshops | Hopkins Center for the Arts at Dartmouth
facts.commonnessReason: A well-known Hopkins Center resource for hands-on making.

facts.title: Carl E. Renshaw, Professor of Earth Sciences
facts.summary: A hydrologist who studies how rivers and streams respond to disturbances such as large floods, climate change, dams, dam removal, and industrial and agricultural legacy contaminants.
facts.hook: studies how rivers respond to floods, climate change, dam removal, and legacy contaminants
facts.quote: I am a hydrologist with research interests in the response of rivers and streams to disturbance -- whether the disturbance is natural (e.g. large floods and climate change) or anthropogenic (e.g. dams, dam removal, and industrial and agricultural legacy contaminants).
facts.sourceTitle: Carl E. Renshaw | Department of Earth and Planetary Sciences

facts.title: Erin Mayfield, Hodgson Family Assistant Professor of Engineering
facts.summary: An engineering professor whose research in sustainable systems engineering and public policy covers energy and industrial systems planning, climate change mitigation, and multi-attribute decision-making.
facts.hook: researches energy systems planning and climate mitigation at the line between engineering and public policy
facts.quote: Erin Mayfield's research is in the areas of sustainable systems engineering and public policy. She focuses on three interacting research themes: energy and industrial systems planning, climate change mitigation, and multi-attribute decision-making.
facts.sourceTitle: Erin Mayfield | Hodgson Family Assistant… | Dartmouth Engineering

facts.title: Klaus Keller, Hodgson Distinguished Professor of Engineering
facts.summary: An engineering professor who studies climate risk management, mitigation and adaptation, robust decision making, and flood risk, aiming to design sustainable risk management strategies.
facts.hook: studies how to design risk management strategies for a changing climate, including flood risk
facts.quote: Second, how can we use this information to design sustainable, scientifically sound, technologically feasible, economically efficient, and ethically defensible risk management strategies? ... Climate risk management; climate change mitigation and adaptation; multisector dynamics; robust decision making; flood risk
facts.sourceTitle: Klaus Keller | Hodgson Distinguished… | Dartmouth Engineering

facts.title: Taylor Ho Bynum, Director, Coast Jazz Orchestra at Dartmouth
facts.summary: The cornetist and composer who directs the Coast Jazz Orchestra and whose Acoustic Bicycle Tours have him traveling to concerts solely by bike.
facts.hook: leads the jazz orchestra as a cornetist and composer who tours to concerts by bicycle
facts.quote: Director, Coast Jazz Orchestra at Dartmouth ... Bynum's expressionistic playing on cornet and his expansive vision as composer have garnered him critical attention on over twenty recordings as a bandleader and dozens more as a sideman. His varied endeavors include his Acoustic Bicycle Tours (where he travels to concerts solely by bike across thousands of miles)
facts.sourceTitle: Taylor Ho Bynum | Hopkins Center for the Arts at Dartmouth

facts.title: Analog Lab at Dartmouth
facts.summary: A lab that designs highly efficient analog and mixed-signal circuits for sensor interfaces in wearable biomedical devices that need quality sensor data at very low power.
facts.hook: designs low-power circuits that read sensors in wearable health devices
facts.quote: The primary goal of our work is to design highly-efficient analog and mixed signal integrated circuits for sensor interfaces in wearable biomedical devices. Many of these devices simultaneously require high quality sensor data and very low power consumption.
facts.sourceTitle: Analog Lab at Dartmouth – Nonlinear Analog Integrated Circuits and Systems

facts.title: Citrin Family GIS/Applied Spatial Analysis Lab
facts.nameOnPage: Citrin Family GIS/Applied Spatial Analysis Lab
facts.summary: A GIS and remote sensing lab whose GPS units, photogrammetric workstations, and field spectrometer students and faculty have used for mapping and field measurements such as turbidity.
facts.hook: supports student GIS, mapping, and remote sensing work with GPS units, photogrammetric workstations, and a field spectrometer
facts.quote: Dartmouth's Citrin Family GIS/Applied Spatial Analysis Lab supports research and education in geographic information science and technology, remote sensing, spatial analysis, geographic data visualization, and related fields. ... Students and faculty have used the lab's GPS units for mapping projects, mobile photogrammetric workstations for offsite work, and our field spectrometer for measuring turbidity in a Svalbard fjord
facts.sourceTitle: Citrin Family GIS / Applied Spatial Analysis Lab at Dartmouth College – Geographic information science and technology

facts.title: DALI Lab
facts.summary: A student lab where small teams of developers, designers, and project managers build apps, VR/AR experiences, games, and data visualizations for partners.
facts.hook: puts students on small teams that build apps and data visualizations for real partners
facts.quote: At DALI (founded 2013), students work in small teams to solve big problems brought to the lab by partners from around the world. Student teams (software engineers, designers, project manager) follow the DALI process to build mobile tools, such as mobile and web applications, VR/AR interactive experiences, games, data visualizations, animations, and more.
facts.sourceTitle: E.E. Just DALI Internship | E.E. Just Program for STEM Advancement
facts.commonnessReason: A well-known student technology lab among computing applicants.

facts.title: Empower Lab
facts.summary: A lab that co-creates inclusive technologies with communities, combining human-computer interaction, personal informatics, social computing, and AI to support health and behavior change.
facts.hook: co-designs inclusive technology with communities to support health, accessibility, and sustainability
facts.quote: We co-create inclusive technologies with communities, combining human–computer interaction, personal informatics, social computing, and AI to support health and behavior change. Through research, design, and real-world deployment, we advance health equity, accessibility, and sustainability to empower individuals and communities.

facts.title: Fallout RadioNuclide Analytics
facts.summary: A gamma spectroscopy lab that uses radionuclide chronometers to study modern change in atmospheric aerosols, forest ecosystems, landscapes, and river systems.
facts.hook: uses radionuclide tracers to measure change in rivers, forests, landscapes, and the atmosphere
facts.quote: This is a gamma spectroscopy lab where we use a suite of fallout radionuclide (FRN) and short-lived radionuclide (SLR) chronometers to understand modern change to atmospheric aerosols, forest ecosystems, physical landscapes, river systems, and the biogeochemical connections among them.
facts.sourceTitle: Fallout RadioNuclide Analytics | Department of Earth and Planetary Sciences

facts.title: Appalachian Trail and Connecticut River
facts.summary: The Appalachian Trail runs through campus and the Connecticut River is just steps away, so outdoor activities are always within reach.
facts.hook: puts the Appalachian Trail and the Connecticut River within steps of campus
facts.quote: With the Appalachian Trail running through campus and the Connecticut River just steps away, outdoor activities are always accessible here.
facts.sourceTitle: Life in the Upper Valley | Dartmouth
facts.commonnessReason: A hallmark of Dartmouth's setting that many applicants mention.

facts.title: Dartmouth Skiway
facts.summary: One of only a handful of U.S. ski areas owned by a college, the Dartmouth Skiway also serves as a ski resource for the wider Upper Valley community.
facts.hook: gives students a college-owned ski area that also serves the Upper Valley community
facts.quote: One of only a handful of American ski areas owned by colleges or universities, the Skiway has become a ski resource for the entire Upper Valley community.
facts.commonnessReason: A known Dartmouth amenity that outdoors-minded applicants mention.

facts.title: Second College Grant
facts.summary: A 27,000-acre woodland given to the College by New Hampshire in 1807 and managed for wilderness recreation, timber that funds scholarships, education, and research.
facts.hook: offers a 27,000-acre college woodland used for wilderness recreation, education, and research
facts.quote: Dartmouth's most visited woodland is a 27,000 acre parcel called the Second College Grant or "the Grant", given to the College by the State of New Hampshire in 1807. ... The Grant has long been recognized as a model forest; one which balances wilderness recreation, timber harvesting that provides revenue for student scholarship, and a sustainably managed forest that supports education and research at Dartmouth

facts.title: Energy Engineering Concentration (Energy Engineering Program Area)
facts.summary: Within the engineering sciences degree, students may choose an energy engineering concentration that also considers social, political, and economic contexts.
facts.hook: lets engineering students concentrate in energy while weighing its social, political, and economic contexts
facts.quote: Within their engineering sciences degree, students may choose a concentration in energy engineering. The Energy Engineering Program Area provides structure and guidance for this concentration involving not only application of the full spectrum of engineering disciplines but also recognition of the social, political, and economic contexts with particular emphasis on human-centered impact.
facts.sourceTitle: Energy Engineering Program Area | Dartmouth Engineering

facts.title: Engineering Sciences Major Modified with Environmental Sciences
facts.summary: A modified Engineering Sciences major that combines engineering courses with environmental science courses drawn from biology, chemistry, ecology, and earth sciences.
facts.hook: lets an engineering major build in environmental science courses from biology, chemistry, and earth sciences
facts.quote: Modified Major with Environmental Sciences: Students interested in engineering and environmental science may elect an engineering major modified with environmental science courses. Effective preparation for graduate study or professional activity in the environmental sciences requires an assimilation of material traditionally encountered in biology, chemistry, ecology, and earth sciences, as well as in engineering sciences.

facts.title: Engineering Sciences Major Modified with Public Policy
facts.summary: A modified Engineering Sciences major for students interested in technology and public policy, with policy tracks that include environment, natural resources, health, and science and technology.
facts.hook: pairs an engineering major with public policy coursework, including an environment and public policy track
facts.quote: Modified major with Public Policy: Students interested in technology and public policy may elect an engineering major modified with public policy. ... Possible tracks include: Environment and Public Policy; Health and Public Policy; Natural resources and Public Policy; and Science/technology and Public Policy.

facts.title: Environmental Studies Major and Minors
facts.summary: The Environmental Studies department offers a major plus minors in Environmental Studies (with Sustainability and Sustainable Energy tracks) and Environmental Science.
facts.hook: offers an Environmental Studies major and minors with Sustainability and Sustainable Energy tracks
facts.quote: To meet the needs of our students, we offer a major in Environmental Studies and two minors: Environmental Studies (tracks available in Environmental Studies, Sustainability or Sustainable Energy) and Environmental Science.
facts.commonnessReason: The main environmental major, so environmentally minded applicants often name it.

facts.title: Coast Jazz Orchestra at Dartmouth
facts.summary: Dartmouth's jazz orchestra, open by audition to students of any major and any instrument, alongside smaller Music Department combos.
facts.hook: lets students of any major audition for the jazz orchestra, alongside smaller Music Department combos
facts.quote: The Coast Jazz Orchestra is open to anyone and any instrument by audition. Students don't have to be a music major or minor, and in addition to the jazz orchestra, the Music Department has several active smaller combos, so hopefully all students can find a context to keep playing that fits their interests and commitment level.
facts.sourceTitle: Coast Jazz Orchestra at Dartmouth | Hopkins Center for the Arts at Dartmouth
facts.commonnessReason: The college's main jazz ensemble, which musically active applicants often mention.

facts.title: Dartmouth Bikes
facts.summary: A student-run campus bike shop that repairs, rents, and refurbishes bikes and trains students to become bike mechanics.
facts.hook: trains students as bike mechanics in a student-run shop that repairs, rents, and refurbishes bikes
facts.quote: Our student-run bike shop repairs, rents, refurbishes all bikes on campus! Get your bike tuned up by one of our skilled student mechanics, or get trained to be a bike mechanic yourself!

facts.title: Dartmouth Cycling
facts.summary: Dartmouth's collegiate cycling team, which races road from mid-March through May and mountain and cyclocross from September to December, and welcomes riders without racing experience.
facts.hook: welcomes riders new to racing onto a team that races road, mountain, and cyclocross
facts.quote: We are always excited when people who lack experience get on a bike and give racing a try. Collegiate racing is a great place to start. ... The collegiate road season runs from mid-March through May. A smaller subset of the team also races mountain and cyclocross from September to December.
facts.sourceTitle: Dartmouth Cycling | Riding Bikes Fast since 1961

facts.title: Dartmouth Forensic Union
facts.summary: Dartmouth's intercollegiate policy debate team, which takes an interdisciplinary approach to debate.
facts.hook: fields Dartmouth's intercollegiate policy debate team
facts.quote: The Dartmouth Forensic Union fields Dartmouth's intercollegiate policy debate team. ... We are committed to an interdisciplinary approach to debate that promotes critical thinking.
facts.commonnessReason: The college's competitive policy debate team, a natural reference for debaters.

facts.title: Dartmouth Formula Racing (DFR)
facts.summary: A student team that designs, builds, and tests a hybrid or electric race car and started the Formula Hybrid+Electric competition that Thayer runs.
facts.hook: has students design, build, and test a hybrid or electric race car
facts.quote: The Dartmouth Formula Racing (DFR) team designs, builds, and tests a high performance hybrid or electric race car. The DFR team initiated the annual Formula Hybrid+Electric™ competition, which is run by Thayer.

facts.title: Dartmouth Humanitarian Engineering (DHE)
facts.summary: A student engineering group that organizes and supports service projects around the world aimed at socially conscious, economically feasible, and sustainable solutions.
facts.hook: organizes engineering service initiatives that aim for socially conscious, economically feasible, sustainable solutions
facts.quote: Dartmouth Humanitarian Engineering (DHE) organizes and supports service initiatives all over the world with the goal of improving a community's quality of life with solutions that are socially conscious, economically feasible, and fully sustainable.

facts.title: Dartmouth Organic Farm Club
facts.summary: A student-run club that organizes educational, social, and volunteer activities at the Organic Farm, on campus, and in the Upper Valley, with no farming experience required.
facts.hook: organizes educational, social, and volunteer activities at the farm and in the Upper Valley, no farming experience needed
facts.quote: Our student-run Farm Club is not just about farming! The Farm Club organizes educational, social, and volunteer opportunities at the O Farm, on campus, and in the Upper Valley. ... The Farm Club is open to any and all who are interested in getting involved! No farming or gardening experience is required.

facts.title: Dartmouth Outing Club
facts.summary: The largest and oldest collegiate outing club in the country, which sponsors outdoor recreation and environmental stewardship.
facts.hook: sponsors outdoor recreation and environmental stewardship through the country's oldest collegiate outing club
facts.quote: The largest and oldest collegiate outing club in the country, the DOC sponsors outdoor recreation and environmental stewardship.
facts.commonnessReason: One of Dartmouth's signature institutions and among the most cited details in Why Dartmouth essays.

facts.title: The Dartmouth
facts.summary: The student newspaper, founded in 1799, which the college describes as the first collegiate newspaper in America.
facts.hook: lets students join the first collegiate newspaper in America, founded in 1799
facts.quote: Founded in 1799, The Dartmouth is the first collegiate newspaper in America.
facts.commonnessReason: Well known on campus and to applicants interested in journalism.

facts.title: Biology Foreign Studies Program (Costa Rica and the Caribbean)
facts.summary: A full-immersion biology program in which students study tropical forests and freshwater ecosystems in Costa Rica and coral reef ecosystems in the Caribbean.
facts.hook: immerses students in the study of tropical forests and freshwater in Costa Rica and Caribbean coral reefs
facts.quote: The Biology Foreign Studies Program (BIOL 55, BIOL 56, BIOL 57) exposes students, through intensive, full-immersion study, to Earth's most diverse biological communities. BIOL 56 is a continuation of BIOL 55; these courses comprise the first two-thirds of the FSP, and focus on land (tropical forests) and tropical freshwater ecosystems in Costa Rica. BIOL 57 focuses on coral reef ecosystems in the Caribbean.

facts.title: Dartmouth as Living Lab
facts.summary: A sustainability initiative that uses Dartmouth's campus lands and infrastructure as test sites for research, teaching, and pilots of climate and sustainability solutions.
facts.hook: turns campus lands and buildings into test sites for climate and sustainability research and pilots
facts.quote: Embracing a "Campus as Lab" approach allows students, faculty, and staff collaborate to use our campus to generate research, teaching, and creative scholarship on climate change and sustainability. Campus lands, infrastructure, and spaces become dynamic testing grounds where innovative sustainability solutions are piloted in real time.
facts.sourceTitle: DARTMOUTH AS LIVING LAB | Dartmouth Sustainability

facts.title: Environmental Studies Africa Foreign Study Program (Namibia)
facts.summary: An Environmental Studies foreign study program that travels to Namibia to study environmental issues in the context of southern Africa, open to students of all majors.
facts.hook: takes students of any major to Namibia to study environmental themes in southern Africa
facts.quote: We also offer the Africa Foreign Study Program that travels to Namibia where we explore the themes of environmental studies within the particular environment, culture and history of the southern Africa region. ... The program benefits from having diverse perspectives among the student participants, and all majors are welcome to apply.

facts.title: First Year Research in Engineering Experience (FYREE)
facts.nameOnPage: First Year Research in Engineering Experience
facts.summary: A paid research internship that pairs first-year students and prospective engineering majors with engineering faculty to take part in active research in their labs.
facts.hook: pairs first-year students with engineering faculty for a paid research internship in their labs
facts.quote: The First Year Research in Engineering Experience (FYREE) program is a paid research internship that provides early hands-on research experience and mentoring within the engineering sciences for first-year Dartmouth undergraduate students and prospective engineering majors. ... During the program, FYREE students are paired with engineering faculty and take part in active research in their labs.
facts.sourceTitle: First Year Research in Engineering Experience | Dartmouth Engineering

facts.title: LALAC House
facts.summary: One of Dartmouth's LLC/affinity houses, devoted to Latin American, Latine, and Caribbean intellectual, social, and cultural life.
facts.hook: offers a residential community centered on Latin American, Latine, and Caribbean culture
facts.quote: LLC/Affinity Houses ... A community devoted to the exploration and expression of traditional and contemporary aspects of Latin American, Latine, and Caribbean intellectual, social and cultural life.
facts.sourceTitle: LLC/Affinity Houses | Office of Pluralism and Leadership

facts.title: Language Study Abroad (LSA and LSA+)
facts.summary: Students can meet the language requirement with two preparatory courses and a term abroad, with LSA and advanced LSA+ programs in countries including Spain, Argentina, Brazil, China, Japan, and Morocco.
facts.hook: lets students complete the language requirement with a term of language study abroad
facts.quote: A student may choose to satisfy the Language Requirement through a combination of two preparatory courses at Dartmouth and one term of study abroad. ... Language Study Abroad (LSA) is available in France, Germany, Italy, Argentina, or Spain. Advanced Language Study Abroad (LSA+) is available in Brazil, China, France, Italy, Japan, Morocco, and Russia.
facts.sourceTitle: Dartmouth College - Language and Advanced Language Study Abroad Program
facts.commonnessReason: A well-known Dartmouth off-campus option among applicants interested in languages.

facts.title: Policy Research Shop
facts.summary: A Rockefeller Center program in which students research policy questions requested by New Hampshire and Vermont state, county, and local government officials.
facts.hook: has students research policy questions for New Hampshire and Vermont state and local officials
facts.quote: The Center sponsors the Policy Research Shop, a student-staffed, faculty-mentored research enterprise in which students conduct research at the request of New Hampshire and Vermont state, county, and local government officials.
facts.sourceTitle: Dartmouth College - The Nelson A. Rockefeller Center for Public Policy

facts.title: Social Impact Practicums (SIPs)
facts.summary: Course-based projects that connect Dartmouth classes with needs identified by Upper Valley nonprofits, including human-centered design projects in Thayer's Senior Design Challenge.
facts.hook: connects coursework to projects for Upper Valley nonprofits, including engineering design projects
facts.quote: A Social Impact Practicum (SIP) is a project-based experiential learning opportunity connecting undergraduate courses at Dartmouth with community needs identified by nonprofit organizations throughout the Upper Valley. ... DCSI also collaborates with Thayer's Senior Design Challenge to match human-centered design projects proposed by Upper Valley nonprofits with this two-term senior-level engineering course.
facts.sourceTitle: Social Impact Practicums (SIPs) | Students | Social Impact

facts.title: Sustainability Action Program (SAP)
facts.summary: A first-year program that teaches how campus food, energy, waste, water, and transportation systems work, then trains teams in design thinking to carry out a campus sustainability project.
facts.hook: trains first-years in design thinking and has teams design and implement a campus sustainability project
facts.quote: The Sustainability Action Program (SAP) is focused on first years ... You will build a solid foundation for understanding how food, energy, waste, water, and transportation work at Dartmouth ... equipping you with tools such as design thinking, systems thinking, and behavior change theory. Then YOU (and a team of fellow SAP-lings) will design and implement a project on a topic you care about that makes Dartmouth even greener!

facts.title: The Stretch
facts.summary: A roughly two-month off-campus field program across the western United States and Canada in which students collect and analyze field data.
facts.hook: takes students on a roughly two-month field traverse of the western U.S. and Canada to collect and analyze data
facts.quote: The Stretch is among the most storied and longest-lived off-campus programs at Dartmouth, and it consists of a roughly two-month traverse across the western United States and Canada where students are directly engaged in field-based data collection and analysis.
facts.sourceTitle: The Stretch | Department of Earth and Planetary Sciences

facts.title: Undergraduate Research Assistantships at Dartmouth (URAD)
facts.summary: A program that funds undergraduates to work as part-time research assistants with Dartmouth faculty, with a stipend paid at the end of each term of research.
facts.hook: pays undergraduates a stipend to work as part-time research assistants with faculty
facts.quote: Undergraduates experience research first-hand by working with Dartmouth faculty in part-time research assistantships. Students receive a stipend at the end of the completed term of research.
facts.sourceTitle: Undergraduate Research Assistantships at Dartmouth (URAD) | Scholars Programs, Undergraduate Research, and Fellowships at Dartmouth
facts.commonnessReason: A broad research-funding program that many science-minded applicants mention.

facts.title: Dartmouth Night and Homecoming
facts.summary: A celebration in which alumni return to join students for a parade and bonfire.
facts.hook: brings alumni back to join students for a parade and bonfire
facts.quote: During Dartmouth Night and Homecoming, alumni return to join students in a revelatory celebration that includes a colorful parade and blazing bonfire.
facts.commonnessReason: A well-known Dartmouth tradition.

facts.title: First-Year Trips
facts.summary: A tradition involving over 90 percent of first-year students, whose groups spend two nights outdoors and then reconvene at the Ravine Lodge on Mt. Moosilauke.
facts.hook: starts college with an outdoor trip that ends at the Moosilauke Ravine Lodge
facts.quote: Today the program involves over 90 percent of the freshman class and more than two hundred upperclassmen student leaders. ... After two nights in the outdoors, the groups reconvene at the Ravine Lodge at the base of Mt. Moosilauke and are treated to stories from administrators, faculty, or alumni about their own Dartmouth experiences.
facts.commonnessReason: A signature Dartmouth tradition that many applicants mention.

facts.title: Ledyard Canoe Club Trip to the Sea
facts.summary: An annual Ledyard Canoe Club tradition in which seniors paddle the Connecticut River from Hanover to Long Island Sound.
facts.hook: sends seniors paddling down the Connecticut River from Hanover to Long Island Sound
facts.quote: This tradition continues today as the annual Trip to the Sea, which sends seniors traveling down the Connecticut River from Hanover to the Long Island Sound.
facts.sourceTitle: Founding of the Ledyard Canoe Club | Dartmouth

facts.title: Winter Carnival
facts.summary: A Dartmouth cold-weather celebration with indoor and outdoor fun for all.
facts.hook: celebrates winter with indoor and outdoor events for the whole campus
facts.quote: But one thing remains constant: Winter Carnival at Dartmouth is still one of the greatest cold-weather celebrations, with indoor and outdoor fun for all.
facts.commonnessReason: One of Dartmouth's best-known traditions.
